statements.subject: session
statements.description: No mapping exists between a Pipelined-Requests identifier (for the current persistent connection) and an RTSP session ID.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A binding exists between a Pipelined-Requests identifier for the current persistent connection and an RTSP session ID.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there does not exist a mapping and no Session header is included in the request, the responding agent MUST create a binding upon the successful completion of a session creating request, i.e., SETUP.
statements.trigger: SETUP with Pipelined-Requests header completes successfully
actions: create binding between Pipelined-Requests identifier and RTSP session ID

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A binding MUST NOT be created if the request failed to create an RTSP session.
statements.trigger: SETUP with Pipelined-Requests header fails to create session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST delete the Pipelined-Requests identifier and its binding to a session upon the termination of that session.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Upon receiving a request with the Pipelined-Requests header, the responding agent MUST look up if there exists a binding. If the binding exists, then the received request is processed the same way as if it contained the Session header with the found session ID.
actions: look up binding for Pipelined-Requests identifier
process request as if Session header with found session ID is present

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In case the request contains both a Session header and the Pipelined-Requests header, the Pipelined-Requests header MUST be ignored.
statements.trigger: request received with both Session header and Pipelined-Requests header
actions: process request using Session header only

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When responding to any request that contained the Pipelined-Requests header, the server MUST also include the Session header when a binding to a session context exists.
